picks.headline: AMD's new X100 chip lineup puts embedded Ryzen AI 'Strix Halo' into robots
picks.excerpt: AMD unveiled its X100 embedded APU lineup, putting Ryzen AI 'Strix Halo' silicon with Zen 5 CPU and RDNA 3.5 GPU cores into robots and other 'physical AI' machines. The chips are pitched as on-device brains for humanoids and edge devices, competing with Intel's Panther Lake and Nvidia's robotics platforms. It marks AMD's push into the emerging market for embedded edge-AI compute powering autonomous hardware.
picks.rationale: AMD embedding Ryzen AI 'Strix Halo' silicon as the on-device brain for humanoids and edge machines is a fresh, credible signal of the compute layer that will power the next wave of AI hardware — distinct from every published gadgets card.

picks.headline: New Tesla Optimus rival: Leak reveals first details about BYD's AI robot 'Xiao Di'
picks.excerpt: EV giant BYD is reportedly preparing to unveil its own bipedal AI humanoid robot, called Xiao Di, positioning it as a rival to Tesla's Optimus. The robot is expected to make its public debut in August and could soon act as a sales assistant presenting EVs in BYD dealerships. It signals another major manufacturer entering the consumer-facing humanoid robot race.
picks.rationale: A major EV manufacturer entering the humanoid-robot race with a consumer-facing sales-assistant robot is a novel, distinct hardware milestone — no robot story remains in the published gadgets history after Neo shipped 07-27.

picks.headline: BrainCo unveils brain-controlled robot AI platform at WAIC 2026
picks.excerpt: At WAIC 2026, BrainCo demonstrated remotely controlling robotic hands, arms and humanoids using only a user's thoughts, via its brain-computer interface (BCI) and a brain-controlled robot AI platform. The system translates neural signals into precise robot manipulation in real time. It points toward hands-free, thought-driven control as an interface layer for AI-powered robots.
picks.rationale: A working brain-computer interface that drives robots by thought introduces a genuinely new interaction modality — highly relevant to a design org, and a distinct device category from the rest of the set.

picks.headline: My Life With Looki Is a Harbinger of Always-On Recording Glasses to Come
picks.excerpt: CNET's Scott Stein lives with Looki, an almost always-on camera-equipped AI pendant that continuously captures and recalls your day. The wearable embodies the extreme assistive aspirations of memory-logging AI, while surfacing the social discomfort and privacy tension of persistent recording. Stein frames it as a preview of the always-on recording glasses and pendants arriving next.
picks.rationale: A lived-in review of an always-on memory-logging AI pendant surfaces the real UX and privacy tensions of persistent recording — directly actionable design signal, and a distinct wearable category.

picks.headline: Meta Is Rethinking Subscriptions on Its Smart Glasses
picks.excerpt: Meta paused plans to paywall Conversation Focus — the on-glasses AI feature that uses the smart glasses' microphones to help wearers hear a conversation more clearly — after user backlash, though it signaled other AI features could still land behind a subscription. The episode highlights the tension over how always-on AI hardware features get monetized.
picks.rationale: How always-on AI hardware features get monetized is a fresh, actionable question for anyone designing AI products — a distinct policy/monetization angle separate from the smart-glasses reviews already published.
